reference.notes:
`withBase` and `withoutBase` now count the base as present only when it ends on a path-segment boundary. All 555 tests pass, including both new suites, and eslint and `tsc --noEmit` report no problems.

The `src/utils.ts` you gave me had no bodies throwing `not implemented`. Both functions still contained the old plain `startsWith` check, so I changed that check in place.

**What changed** (only `src/utils.ts`):
- I added a private helper, `_hasBase(input, base)`. It is true only when `input` starts with the base exactly (same case, no decoding) and the next character is end of input, `/` or `?`. It isn't exported, so nothing new reaches `src/index.ts`.
- `withBase` and `withoutBase` now use this helper instead of `input.startsWith(_base)`. Everything else in both functions is unchanged: the early returns, `joinURL` and how the base is stripped.

**Effect:**
- `withoutBase("/apiv2", "/api")` now returns `"/apiv2"`; it used to return `"/v2"`.
- `withBase("/apiv2", "/api")` now returns `"/api/apiv2"`; it used to return `"/apiv2"`.
- As the spec decides, `#`, a backslash and a base that still ends in `/` (from `"/api//"`) get no special treatment.
